title: Verify item receives unique canonical identifier on creation
gherkin:
Given a new item is being created
When the item is saved to the system
Then the item should be assigned a unique canonical identifier
And the canonical identifier should be immutable
rationale: Items must have a unique canonical identity assigned upon creation to ensure they can be uniquely identified throughout their lifecycle.

title: Verify canonical identity persists across system updates

Given an item with an established canonical identity
When the item's attributes are updated
Then the canonical identity should remain unchanged
And the item should still be identifiable by its original canonical identifier
rationale: The canonical identity must persist even when item properties change, ensuring consistent identification over time.

title: Verify no two items share the same canonical identity
gherkin:

When comparing their canonical identities

And no two items should share the same canonical identifier
rationale: Canonical identity must be unique across all items to prevent identity conflicts and ensure proper item distinction.
